claims.text: Traditional synthesis methods typically produce noble metal–based HEA precursors with relatively random atomic distributions.
Enhanced free-energy sampling can be integrated into an HEA synthesis protocol to guide nucleation and growth.
Metadynamics can map free-energy barriers relevant to HEA nucleation and growth.
Metadynamics-guided synthesis will direct HEA growth toward a three-dimensional nanoframework architecture.
The proposed intervention modifies the local atomic free-energy landscape.
Modification of the local free-energy landscape promotes preferential nucleation sites.
Preferential nucleation and directed growth mediate the formation of interconnected nanoframeworks.
Mapping and overcoming specific nucleation and growth barriers selectively activates formation of well-defined three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The metadynamics-guided pathway reduces randomness in atomic assembly.
Reduced randomness in atomic assembly leads to improved atomic-scale control.
Metadynamics-guided synthesis will significantly increase the formation of uniform three-dimensional HEA nanoframeworks relative to conventional synthesis.
The resulting nanoframeworks will have enhanced surface area and a more controlled atomic structure.
Enhanced surface area and controlled atomic structure will improve catalytic activity.
Conventional synthesis methods typically yield bulk or irregular HEA nanostructures without precise atomic control.
The proposed approach will be most effective at laboratory scale under controlled nucleation conditions.
Scale-up and variation in alloy composition may reduce the precision of nanoframework formation.
